An Innocent Man is a 1989 American crime drama movie directed by Peter Yates and starring Tom Selleck, F. Murray Abraham, Laila Robins, David Rasche, Richard Young, Bruce A. Young, Badja Djola, Todd Graff. It was distributed by Touchstone Pictures.

An American Tail is a 1986 American animated musical comedy-drama movie directed by Don Bluth and written by Judy Freudberg and Tony Geiss. It stars an ensemble voice cast of Cathianne Blore, Dom DeLuise, John Finnegan, Phillip Glasser, Amy Green, Madeline Kahn, Pat Musick, Nehemiah Persoff, Christopher Plummer, Neil Ross, Will Ryan, Hal Smith, and Erica Yohn. Set in the 19th century, the story centers on Fievel Mousekewitz, a young Russian-Jewish mouse who is separated from his family while emigrating from the Russian Empire to the United States for freedom and must provide a way in reuniting with them. Production on An American Tail began in December 1984 and was originally conceived as a television special, but executive producer Steven Spielberg felt it had potential as a feature movie, and asked Bluth to "make [him] something pretty like [he] did in NIMH." The film was animated at Sullivan Bluth Studios, with James Horner composing the film's score and writing original songs. Upon its theatrical premiere in the United States on November 21, 1986, by Universal Pictures, An American Tail received mixed reviews from critics, and it was an commercial success, grossing $85 million worldwide on a $9 million budget. The success spawned a franchise, including a theatrical sequel, a television series, and two sequels released on home video. In 1885, in Shostka, Russia, the Mousekewitzes are a Russian-Jewish family of mice who live with a human family named Moskowitz. During a Hanukkah celebration, Papa gives his kashket to his son, Fievel, and tells him about the United States, which he believes is a country with no cats. The celebration is interrupted when a group of Cossacks rides through the village square and sets fire to the village as part of an anti-Semitic attack. Their cats also attack the village mice. The Moskowitz and Mousekewitz homes are destroyed, and Fievel narrowly escapes. The Mousekewitzes then flee the village in search of a better life. In Hamburg, Germany, the Mousekewitzes board a tramp steamer bound for New York City. The mice aboard are excited about going to America because they believe that there are no cats there. During a thunderstorm, Fievel is separated from his family and washed overboard. Believing that he has drowned, his family continues to New York, saddened by his loss. Fievel survives and reaches New York inside a bottle. After receiving encouragement from a French pigeon named Henri, he begins searching for his family. He meets conman Warren T. Rat, who sells him to a sweatshop. Fievel escapes with Tony Toponi, a street-smart Italian mouse. They later meet Bridget, an Irish mouse who is trying to organize the mice against the cats. When the Mott Street Maulers attack a mouse marketplace, the immigrant mice discover that the stories about America being free of cats are false. They also learn that Warren T. Rat has been demanding protection payments from the mice. Bridget takes Fievel and Tony to meet Honest John, an alcoholic politician who knows many of the city's voting mice. However, he cannot help Fievel find his family because they have not yet registered to vote. Led by the wealthy Gussie Mausheimer, the mice hold a meeting to decide how to deal with the cats and Warren's demands. Fievel secretly tells Gussie about a plan. Although the Mousekewitzes attend the meeting, they sit at the back and do not recognize Fievel when he appears on stage. The mice occupy an abandoned museum on the Chelsea Piers and begin preparing their plan. On the day of the operation, Fievel becomes lost and discovers Warren's hideout. He learns that Warren is actually a cat in disguise and the leader of the Mott Street Maulers. The gang captures Fievel and imprisons him. His guard, Tiger, is a reluctant vegetarian tabby cat who befriends Fievel and helps him escape. Fievel returns to the pier while being pursued by the cats. He reveals Warren's true identity just as Gussie orders the mice to activate their secret weapon. The weapon is a large mechanical mouse based on Papa's bedtime stories about the "Giant Mouse of Minsk". It chases Warren and the Maulers down the pier and into the water. A tramp steamer bound for Hong Kong catches the cats on its anchor and carries them away. A fire starts on the pier after leaking kerosene cans cause a torch lying on the ground to ignite. The mice flee when the fire department arrives. During the chaos, Fievel is separated from his family again and ends up at an orphanage in an alley. Papa and Tanya hear Bridget and Tony calling for Fievel. Papa initially believes that there must be another mouse named Fievel, but Mama recognizes Fievel's hat. With Gussie's help, and with Tiger carrying them, they search for Fievel and find him. Papa returns Fievel's hat to him and realizes that he has grown and that the hat now fits him. Henri then takes the Mousekewitzes and their friends to see his newly completed project, the Statue of Liberty. As they look at the statue, it appears to smile and wink at Fievel and Tanya. The Mousekewitzes begin their new life in the United States. Phillip Glasser as Fievel Mousekewitz. (Cf. Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz and Feivel Gruberger). The main protagonist, he is the only son of Papa and Mama Mousekewitz. A high-spirited, daring yet naïve Russian-Jewish mouse, Fievel becomes a frightened child when he is separated from his family. The strength and the encouragement from his new American friends from Henri to Tony and Bridget give him the strength to reach his goal in reuniting with his family while starting a new life in America. While "Fievel" is the usual spelling of his name, the opening credits spell it as "Feivel", the more common transliteration of the Yiddish name (פֿײַװל Fayvl). Feivel was the same name of Steven Spielberg's grandfather, whose stories as an immigrant influenced the film. However, many English-speaking writers use spelling Fievel, especially for this character; it was this spelling that was used on the film's poster, in promotional materials and tie-in merchandise, and in the title of the sequel An American Tail: Fievel Goes West. His last name is a play on the Russian-Jewish last name "Moskowitz", the name of the human occupants of the house his family is living under in the beginning of the film. John Finnegan as Warren T. Rat, a small Havana Brown who disguises himself as a rat. He is the leader of the Mott Street Maulers, an all-cat gang which terrorizes the mice of New York City. Conniving and a schemer, he misleads the gullible Fievel at one point. Later on, he gets his comeuppance when Fievel discovers and later exposes him as a cat to the Mouse community. He is accompanied everywhere by his accountant Digit, a small English-accented cockroach. Amy Green as Tanya Mousekewitz (singing voice provided by Betsy Cathcart), Fievel's older sister, whom he mutually adores. Optimistic and cheerful, less daring but more obedient than her brother, she alone believes (correctly) that he survived being washed overboard en route to the United States. She is given the American name "Tillie" at the immigration point at Castle Garden. Nehemiah Persoff as Papa Mousekewitz, the head of the Mousekewitz family who plays the violin and tells stories to his children. Erica Yohn as Mama Mousekewitz, Fievel's mother. Countering Papa's dreamy idealism, she is a level-headed pragmatist, besides being stricter with their offspring than he is. She also has a fear of flying. Pat Musick as Tony Toponi, a streetwise teenage mouse of Italian descent. His "tough guy" attitude suits his New York surroundings. The name "Toponi" is a play on "topo", the Italian word for "mouse". He hits it off with Fievel, acting as a surrogate big brother to the younger mouse, whom he calls "Philly". In a subplot, he falls in love with Bridget. Dom DeLuise as Tiger, the most physically imposing member of the Mott Street Maulers, whom he serves as an enforcer, and often as the brunt of their cruel jokes. This bushy-tailed, orange long-haired tabby stands 3 feet tall on his rear legs. Although not especially intelligent, Tiger is very friendly, and his warm nature endears him to mice and birds. He is mostly vegetarian, aside from the occasional bit of fish. Tiger becomes Fievel's best friend. He enjoys card games like poker and gin rummy, despite being terrible at them. Tiger's singing voice also helps him stand out; he sings Lyric and Dramatic Bass and Lyric and Dramatic Baritone, from D2 or E2 to F4 or G4. He is a Persian Tabby. Christopher Plummer as Henri le Pigeon, a pigeon of French descent, who oversees construction of the Statue of Liberty. Cathianne Blore as Bridget, an attractive, elegant Irish-born mouse and Tony's significant other. Her parents were slain and devoured by the Mott Street Maulers, making her an advocate in speaking out against the cats. Kind, passionate yet soft-spoken, she acts as a surrogate big sister to Fievel. Neil Ross as Honest John, a local Irish-born mouse politician who knows every voting mouse in New York City. An ambulance-chasing drunkard, he takes advantage of voters' concerns to increase his political prestige. John is a caricature of real-life Tammany Hall boss John Kelly (also nicknamed "Honest John") and other 19th-century New York City politicians. Madeline Kahn as Gussie Mausheimer, a German-born mouse considered to be the richest in New York City, who rallies the mice into fighting back against the cats. Despite being against cats, she later accepts Tiger for helping to reunite Fievel with his family. Will Ryan as Digit, Warren's British cockroach accountant who has a fondness for counting money but is plagued by frequent electrical charges in his antennae whenever he gets nervous or excited. Hal Smith as Moe, a fat rat who runs the local sweatshop. Fievel is sold to him by Warren. Dan Kuenster as Jake, Warren's burly aide-de-camp. Among the Mott Street Maulers, he alone enjoys listening to his leader's violin music. Jake catches Fievel after a chase through the sewers. After Tiger takes pity on Fievel and sets him free, Jake and his fellow Maulers pursue the young mouse to the Chelsea Pier, only to face the "Giant Mouse of Minsk".

An Almost Perfect Affair is a 1979 American romantic comedy movie directed by Michael Ritchie and starring Keith Carradine, Monica Vitti, Raf Vallone, Christian De Sica, Dick Anthony Williams, Katya Berger, Andy Ho, Susan Gilmore. It was distributed by Paramount Pictures.

An Awful Moment is a 1908 American silent drama movie directed by D. W. Griffith and stars George Gebhardt, Marion Leonard, and Harry Solter. An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success is a 2015 family comedy-drama direct-to-video movie starring Olivia Rodrigo, Virginia Madsen, Eloise Webb, Caitlin Carmichael, Notlim Taylor, Lili Bordán, Fabrice Michel, Roxane Bret, Krisztina Peremartoni and András Bálint. An American Tail: Fievel Goes West is a 1991 American animated musical comedy-drama movie directed by Phil Nibbelink and Simon Wells. It is the sequel to the 1986 movie An American Tail.

An American Tail: The Treasure of Manhattan Island is a 1998 American animated musical comedy-drama movie directed by Larry Latham. It is the sequel to the 1991 movie An American Tail: Fievel Goes West.

An American Tail: The Mystery of the Night Monster is a 1999 American animated musical comedy-drama movie directed by Larry Latham. It is the sequel to the 1998 movie An American Tail: The Treasure of Manhattan Island. After the events of the third film, Fievel's sister Tanya and his friend Tony start working for a local newspaper. Fievel has nightmares about mysterious attacks on mice in New York City. He believes a monster is taking mice away at night. The Mousekewitz family and Tony meet Nellie Brie, a reporter who investigates corruption and injustice. Tony wants to become a reporter, but editor Reed Daley gives him simple jobs. Tanya works as Reed's secretary and has a crush on him. Fievel helps Nellie investigate the disappearances and draws pictures of the monster based on witnesses' stories. Reed creates stories about a monster living under Manhattan to sell more newspapers. However, the disappearances are real. A small dog named Madame Mousey appears at the crime scenes and claims to be a fortune teller. She sells mice objects that she says will protect them from the monster. Nellie, Fievel and Tony discover that Mousey is behind the attacks. She works with a gang of cats, who capture mice in the sewers and keep them in cages. The monster is actually a machine created by Mousey to frighten and capture the mice. Mousey learns that the newspaper is going to expose her plan. She repairs the damaged machine and orders the cats to attack the newspaper office. She also attacks mice across the city. Fievel discovers that his family has disappeared and finds them trapped in the sewers with the other captured mice. Fievel returns to the newspaper office for help. There, Mousey and her cats have trapped Nellie, Reed and Tanya. Fievel overcomes his fear of the monster and discovers that it is only a machine. He uses exposed electrical wires to stop Mousey, allowing the others to escape. Tony floods the sewers with water, allowing the captured mice to escape. Tiger brings the dog council to the newspaper office, and the dogs chase away the cats and arrest Mousey. At the beach, Tanya is still sad because Reed has fallen in love with Nellie. Fievel's father tells him that helping Nellie find the monster also helped him find courage. The dog council decides to return Mousey to her former owner instead of sending her to prison. With the mystery solved, Fievel finally falls asleep beside his family. The Mousekewitz family, Tony and Tiger share a group hug and wish him sweet dreams.

It stars Stuart Whitman, Janet Leigh, Eleanor Parker, Lloyd Nolan, Murray Hamilton, Les Crane and Warren Stevens. It was distributed by Warner Bros. and was nominated for an Academy Award in 1967.

An Unmarried Woman is a 1978 American comedy drama movie directed and written by Paul Mazursky. It stars Jill Clayburgh, Alan Bates, Michael Murphy, Cliff Gorman and was distributed by 20th Century Fox. It was nominated for three Oscars in 1979.

An anachronism is a person or thing that is out of place in time. The term is often used in movies or television program when they show a person using something that wasn't invented yet. For example, in the movie The Green Mile, which is set in 1935, they are shown using an electric chair, which wasn't used until 1940.

Anaconda is a 2025 American action comedy horror movie. It was released on December 25, 2025. It was directed by Tom Gormican and produced by Brad Fuller and Andrew Form. It is a meta-reboot of the 1997 movie of the same name. It is also the seventh installment in the Anaconda film series. It follows a group of friends who decide to shoot a remake of their favourite movie in the jungle and come across a massive anaconda. Additionally, Jennifer Lopez, who appeared in the original Anaconda film, has an uncredited cameo appearance as herself. Principal photography began on January 2025 in Australia and finished in early March. Anaconda had its world premiere in Los Angeles on December 13, 2025. It was released in the United States on December 25, 2025, by Sony Pictures Releasing. The film was released on digital on January 27, 2026, and on DVD on March 17, 2026, by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment.

Anadolu Kartalları (Anatolian Eagles) is a 2011 Turkish romantic adventure drama movie directed by Ömer Vargı and starring Engin Altan Düzyatan, Çağatay Ulusoy, Özge Özpirinçci, Hande Subaşı, Ekin Türkmen.

Anaconda is a 1997 American adventure horror movie. It was directed by Luis Llosa and written by Hans Bauer, Jim Cash and Jack Epps Jr.. It starred with Jennifer Lopez, Ice Cube, Jon Voight, Eric Stoltz, Jonathan Hyde and Owen Wilson. It focuses on a documentary film crew in the Amazon rainforest that is captured by a snake hunter who is hunting down a giant, legendary green anaconda. The movie received mostly negative reviews but was a box office success. It grossed $136.8 million worldwide against a $45 million budget. It also became a cult classic. It was followed by a series of films. Frank Welker and Gary A. Hecker as the voices of the Anaconda snake characters.

Anak-ku Sazali is a 1956 Singaporean Malay-language black-and-white melodrama film directed and written by Phani Majumdar. The movie is about love between a man and a woman, dreams that come true, and a father's extreme love for his son. The talented P. Ramlee plays the father, Hassan, and the spoiled son, Sazali Hassan. Hassan, an orphan, works for a rich family. The family has two children, Mansor and Mahani. Hassan loves music and buys a violin, taking lessons to learn how to play. He becomes close friends with Mansor and Mahani. As adults, Mansor goes to Singapore to study, and Mahani is arranged to be married. Hassan, in love with Mahani, flees to Singapore, and Mahani follows him. They meet Mansor at the train station, and he supports their love. Hassan and Mahani marry with Mansor's consent, and Mansor marries a girl named Rubiah. Hassan becomes a famous musician. One day, Mahani collapses and a doctor reveals she is pregnant. Hassan is delighted but Mahani fears she will die during childbirth. She makes Hassan promise to take care of their child. Hassan composes a song, "Anakku Sazali," for the baby. Mahani goes into labor and dies after giving birth to a son, Sazali. Hassan is devastated but dedicates himself to raising Sazali. Hassan spoils Sazali, who grows up to be selfish and mischievous. Sazali lies and steals, causing trouble at school and in the neighborhood. Despite warnings from Mansor, Hassan refuses to discipline him harshly. Sazali becomes a leader of a gang in Singapore. On his birthday, Sazali assaults and impregnates Mansor's daughter, Rokiah, but refuses to marry her. This angers Hassan, who confronts and slaps Sazali. Sazali blames his father's excessive love for his misdeeds and leaves home. Sazali plans a robbery but is caught by the police during a gunfight. He escapes and hides at Hassan's house. Hassan, heartbroken and realizing his mistakes, calls the police. Sazali is arrested, and Hassan prays for forgiveness for both himself and his son. Daeng Idris as Mr. Sulong, school principal Malek Sutan Muda as Mansur & Mahani's father Omar Suwita as members of the Sazali gang Jins Shamsuddin as while at the train station

The film is a sequel to Anacondas 3: Offspring (2008) and the fourth installment in the Anaconda film series. It premiered on the Sci-Fi Channel on February 28, 2009.

Analog television is broadcasting television programming using analog signals. Before digital television, all broadcasters used analog signals. Analog television can be wireless or can be over a cable television network. Many countries have changed from analog to digital television. Others are in the process of changing, and some have not started changing. In 2008, the FCC in the US said that all full power stations needed to switch to digital by the 13th of February 2009. Most had already been running digital channels alongside the analog version. Satellite, cable, and users with low power did not need to make the change at the time. The FCC gave people up to two $40 coupons to buy converter boxes between January 2008 and March 2009. In the UK, regions began changing to digital terrestrial television in 2007. The regional phase ended in 2012. Northern Ireland was the last place to replace analog in the UK on the morning of the 24th of October, 2012. Some people were worried that because some digital channels didn't have subtitles, that some people would have difficulty understanding what was happening. The London Olympic Games were meant to be held soon, which also made people worried that the timetable would affect people's ability to watch it if they did not make the switch completely. Meanwhile, in the US, two years after all of the full-power analog TV stations were shut down, the FCC, on July 15, 2011, made the schedule for low-power television. The last ones were in Alaska and converted in January 2022.

Anastasia is a movie made in 1956 by 20th Century Fox. The movie was directed by Anatole Litvak. The movie stars Ingrid Bergman, Yul Brynner, and Helen Hayes. Other players include Akim Tamiroff (who earlier worked with Ingrid Bergman in the movie For Whom the Bell Tolls), Martita Hunt (who has a comic part as a fussy lady-in-waiting), and, in a small role, Natalie Schafer (familiar to television audiences from her later role on Gilligan's Island). This movie was one of many European movies directed by Litvak into the 1950s and 1960s. It earned an Academy Award for Bergman, who did more movies after this movie. It was nominated for a BAFTA Award for Best British Screenplay. The movie is based upon the story of Grand Duchess Anastasia Nikolaevna of Russia. The youngest daughter of Tsar Nicholas II, Anastasia was brutally murdered along with her parents and siblings by the Bolsheviks, in an attempt to prevent them from reclaiming power, should they ever escape from captivity. Despite the testimony of Yakov Mikhailovich Yurovsky and others present at the shooting, many failed to believe that every member of the family had been killed. This rumor was made worse by stories of one or more of them escaping, thanks to sympathetic guards at Ipatiev House, Yekaterinburg, where they were being held. Also complicating the truth was the fact the location of the bodies remained a mystery, as they had been burned and buried in a remote forest. With rumors swirling that one or more of the Romanovs might have escaped, numerous individuals came forward claiming to be one of the Grand Duchesses or Tsarevich Alexei Nikolaevich. The most notable of these was Anna Anderson, who rose to fame in the 1920s with her outlandish claims that she was Anastasia. The movie was most certainly based on Anderson's story, as the opening shots show a woman about to commit suicide from a bridge, as Anna Anderson did. While Anderson vehemently stated she was the heir to the Romanov family, many around her had doubts. Nevertheless, her story was immensely popular with the public. While the movie hints that Anna was in fact Anastasia, it is now proved beyond a doubt that Anderson was an impostor. With the final resting places of the Romanovs were discovered in 1991 and 2008, all of their bodies have been accounted for. Additionally, DNA tests conducted on the bodies prove that all were members of the Romanov family. Further, DNA testing on a piece of Anderson's intestine that had been saved during an operation she had during the early 1980s proved that she was not a Romanov, but most likely Franziska Schanzkowska, a Polish factory worker with a history of mental illness. Nevertheless, doubt still persisted. Several strands of her hair were discovered in a book, which was also tested. This too proved she was not a member of the royal family and also increased the likelihood that she was Schanzkowska. The movie tells the story of a young, confused woman in 1920s France, played by Ingrid Bergman. She is found by a group of Russian people who have left their country. They want her to pretend to the world that she is Anastasia, in order to retrieve her inheritance. The real Anastasia, if she were alive, would inherit millions of pounds which had been left in an English bank by the Tsar. The Russians, led by General Bounine (played by Yul Brynner), teach her how to behave as the Grand Duchess Anastasia would. They teach her everything she ought to know about her childhood. They teach her to walk like a Duchess, practicing with a book on her head. When they think she is ready, she is introduced to several people who knew Anastasia. None of them believe she really is Anastasia. The real test comes when she is taken by General Bounine (Brynner) to Denmark to meet the Dowager Empress, Maria Feodorovna, mother of the Tsar, played by Helen Hayes. At first the old Empress does not believe the young woman is her granddaughter, but when Anastasia coughs because she is nervous, the Empress remembers that Anastasia used to do this as a child. She now believes she is her granddaughter. Meanwhile, Prince Paul wants to marry Anastasia. He's obviously after the money he thinks she will inherit. In the final scene, there is a party. The Dowager Empress is going to announce the engagement between Paul and Anastasia, but Anastasia and General Bounine have suddenly disappeared. The Dowager realizes that Anastasia does not desire fame, but simply love, with the man of her choosing. She says very bravely that she will go in to where all the guests are waiting and tell them that the party is over and that they should go home. An animated musical version of Anastasia was made in 1997 by Fox Animation Studios. See: Anastasia (1997 movie).

Anastasia: The Mystery of Anna (Sometimes called Anastasia: The Story of Anna) is a 1986 Golden Globe and Emmy Award-winning TV movie, starring Amy Irving, Olivia de Havilland, Omar Sharif and Christian Bale. The movie was loosely based on the story of Grand Duchess Anastasia Nikolaevna of Russia and the novel The Riddle of Anna Anderson by Peter Kurth. It was Christian Bale's first movie and was originally broadcast in two parts. The movie is about Anna Anderson, who believes that she is Anastasia, daughter of Nicholas II of Russia. Anna first tells her story in the 1920s when she is at a Berlin psychiatric hospital. Her story of escape from the Bolsheviks who killed the rest of her family in 1918 seems so vivid that many Russians believe her. She slowly gains more trust, but the Romanov family does not believe her. The movie never reveals if Anna really is Anastasia.

Andrea Beaumont, also known as the Phantasm, is a supervillain and antiheroine created by Alan Burnett and Paul Dini and designed by Bruce Timm. She first appeared as the main antagonist in the 1993 animated film Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, which is part of the DC Animated Universe (DCAU). In the film, she is revealed to be the former fiancée of Bruce Wayne, also known as Batman. Dana Delany provides the voice of Andrea Beaumont, while Stacy Keach provides the electronically modified voice of her Phantasm identity. Keach also voices Andrea's father, Carl Beaumont. Beaumont has appeared in several other works set in the DC Animated Universe. In December 2020, she made her main DC Universe comic book debut in Batman/Catwoman, a 12-issue limited series written by Tom King. Bruce Timm designed Andrea Beaumont's civilian appearance to match the visual style of Batman: The Animated Series. The series was influenced by film noir and used a style known as "Dark Deco". Her appearance was based on women's fashion from the 1940s. She has red hair in a long bob, similar to that of actress Lauren Bacall. Her clothing includes sweaters associated with the "sweater girl" style, high-waisted pencil skirts, wrap dresses, and high-heeled shoes. Timm designed the Phantasm's costume based on Alan Burnett's description of a character resembling the Grim Reaper. Burnett wanted the character to look like the Ghost of Christmas Future from A Christmas Carol. The Joker refers to this resemblance in the film. Timm created about 20 different designs before settling on the final version. Five alternative costume designs were shown in HBO's television preview, "First Look", for Mask of the Phantasm. Timm described the Phantasm as resembling a "tall, gaunt Death character". The costume has a hood and a metal mask shaped like a skull. The Phantasm also carries a large blade similar to a scythe in her right hand. Burnett suggested adding the blade after Timm had created the original design. The Phantasm's left glove contains a device that produces artificial fog through a chemical process. She uses the fog to hide, fight enemies, and frighten people. In some scenes, the fog makes her appear to have supernatural abilities, such as becoming intangible or disappearing. These effects were influenced by Mysterio, a supervillain from Marvel Comics. Stacy Keach provides the Phantasm's voice. His performance was digitally altered to make the voice deeper and add an echo. Parts of his original, unaltered performance can be heard in the theatrical trailer for Mask of the Phantasm. The voice includes the character's signature line, "Your angel of death awaits". The Phantasm's appearances are accompanied by an eerie musical theme composed by Shirley Walker, which prominently features the theremin. The screenplay for Batman: Mask of the Phantasm was written by Alan Burnett, Martin Pasko, Paul Dini, and Michael Reaves. Pasko wrote many of the film's flashback scenes, including those involving Andrea Beaumont and Bruce Wayne. He also wrote the final confrontation between Batman, the Phantasm, and the Joker. Andrea is loosely based on Judson Caspian, also known as the Reaper, and his daughter Rachel. Both characters appeared in the four-issue comic book storyline "Batman: Year Two", which was published in Detective Comics #575–578 in 1987. According to Kevin Conroy, Andrea was named after voice director Andrea Romano. Producer Alan Burnett wanted Mask of the Phantasm to focus on Bruce Wayne's romantic life. He said that the television series had not explored this part of Bruce's life in depth and that he wanted the film to show more of his thoughts and feelings. Burnett described the story as being about "the girl who got away", the woman who might have prevented Bruce from becoming Batman. Andrea's relationship with Bruce became a central part of the film's story and influenced his decision to become Batman. Andrea's role in the film is similar to that of the femme fatale, a common character type in hardboiled detective fiction and film noir. Burnett also wanted the story to move away from Batman's usual group of enemies. The revelation that Andrea is the Phantasm and the main antagonist is an example of a plot twist involving a femme fatale. Andrea also serves as a foil to Batman. Both characters wear intimidating costumes and visit the graves of their parents. Their parents were both killed by criminals, but the two characters respond to these losses in different ways. Andrea becomes a vigilante who kills to take revenge on her father's murderers. Bruce also becomes a vigilante, but follows a moral code that forbids killing. Their similar experiences highlight the different choices they make. Andrea Beaumont is the daughter of wealthy businessman Carl Beaumont and his wife, Victoria. She meets billionaire Bruce Wayne while studying at Gotham University, and the two fall in love. Bruce struggles to choose between his promise to fight crime and his desire to marry Andrea. He believes his parents would have wanted him to find happiness. After trying to stop a truck robbery while wearing a mask and a leather jacket, Bruce decides to marry Andrea and give up fighting crime. He also plans to donate part of his inheritance to the Gotham City Police Department. Bruce takes Andrea to a grotto on his property, which later becomes the Batcave, and proposes to her. She accepts. Andrea later discovers that her father has been working for Mafia boss Sal Valestra and his associates, Chuckie Sol and Buzz Bronski. Carl has created fake companies for the criminals. When they discover that he has stolen some of their money, Carl and Andrea flee to Europe. Andrea ends her engagement to Bruce, who becomes Batman and begins fighting crime. She and her father travel around Europe before settling on the Mediterranean coast. Carl's former lawyer, Arthur Reeves, discovers where the Beaumonts are living. He gives their location to the Mafia in exchange for money to support his campaign for a seat on the Gotham City Council. Although Carl returns the stolen money, the criminals still order his death. They send Jack Napier, who later becomes the Joker, to kill him. Andrea tries to explain that her father has repaid the money, but Napier ignores her. She later finds her father's body. Andrea spends years training to avenge her father's death. She returns to Gotham as the Phantasm, a masked vigilante who uses a smoke generator, a bladed weapon attached to her arm, and a voice changer built into her mask. The device makes her voice sound like her father's. She kills Sol and Bronski. Batman had previously stopped Sol from flooding Gotham with counterfeit money, but he becomes a suspect in the murders. Reeves orders the police to hunt Batman despite Commissioner James Gordon's objections. Andrea visits her mother's grave, where she encounters Batman. She realizes that he is Bruce Wayne but refuses to answer his questions about the murders. Meanwhile, Valestra asks Reeves for protection from Batman. When Reeves cannot help him, Valestra turns to the Joker and asks him to kill Batman. The Phantasm enters Valestra's home to kill him but discovers that the Joker has already murdered him and prepared a trap for Batman. Andrea removes her costume and helps Bruce escape. She claims that the Phantasm is her father and that she is trying to stop him. The two spend the night together. The Joker later confronts Reeves about his past dealings with Valestra. He reveals that the Phantasm, not Batman, is responsible for the murders. He suggests that Reeves either committed the killings himself or hired someone to protect his political career. When Andrea calls Reeves's office to cancel a meeting, the Joker realizes that she may be involved. He poisons Reeves with Joker venom. Batman later visits Reeves and forces him to admit that he betrayed Carl. The Phantasm tracks the Joker to the abandoned Gotham World Fairgrounds. However, the Joker has discovered her identity and prepared for her attack. During their fight, he traps her near a large turbine. Batman intervenes and saves her. Andrea tries to justify her actions by comparing them to Bruce's promise to fight crime, but Batman begs her to abandon her quest for revenge. She disappears in a cloud of smoke. Batman and the Joker continue fighting as explosives destroy the fairgrounds. The Phantasm returns and says, "One way or another, it ends tonight." She captures the Joker and disappears with him. Batman escapes through the sewers and believes that Andrea has died. His butler, Alfred Pennyworth, tells him that Andrea chose her own path and that Bruce could not have changed her decision. Bruce then finds Andrea's locket, which shows that she survived. Meanwhile, Andrea stands alone on the deck of an ocean liner. When a man asks if she wants to be alone, she replies, "I am." Andrea Beaumont first appeared in a comic book adaptation of Batman: Mask of the Phantasm in December 1993. A digest-sized edition was included with the film's VHS release. A full-sized prestige-format edition was also published around the same time. Both editions had the same red cover, while a separate newsstand edition featured a different cover. The Phantasm returned in "Shadow of the Phantasm", a story published in Batman & Robin Adventures Annual #1 in November 1996. The story is a direct sequel to Mask of the Phantasm. Andrea and Batman work together against Arthur Reeves, who seeks revenge on them after the Joker leaves him with a permanent grin. Reeves also discovers that Batman is Bruce Wayne. The story ends with Reeves falling to his death. In 2004, Andrea appeared in Batman Adventures: Shadows and Masks. She goes undercover in the False Face Society, a criminal organization led by Black Mask. During the story, she meets Bruce Wayne at Wayne Manor. Bruce is also undercover, using his criminal identity, Matches Malone. Andrea asks him not to interfere with her mission, but he calls her a killer. She later fights Batgirl and captures her, placing her in a water tank. Bruce rescues Batgirl, and Andrea later attempts to kill Black Mask. Dana Delany, who voiced Andrea Beaumont, later voiced Lois Lane in Superman: The Animated Series. In the three-part crossover story "World's Finest", Lois becomes involved in a love triangle with Superman and Batman. Delany said that Batman was attracted to Lois because she had Andrea's voice. This suggests that Andrea remained important to Bruce, even years after the events of Batman: Mask of the Phantasm. The Phantasm appears briefly in the Justice League Unlimited episode "Epilogue" (2005). Years after Bruce Wayne retires, Amanda Waller hires Andrea to kill the parents of Terry McGinnis and recreate the events that led to Bruce becoming Batman. However, Andrea refuses when she learns what Waller wants her to do. The Phantasm returns in "Mark of the Phantasm", a seven-part story published in the 2015 digital comic Batman Beyond 2.0. The story takes place after the Batman Beyond animated series. Acting on Amanda Waller's orders, Andrea targets Jake Chill, a descendant of Joe Chill who is also known as the Vigilante. Jake is responsible for the murder of Terry McGinnis's father. Andrea is tasked with killing Jake before Terry discovers the truth and considers taking revenge himself. Andrea's first attempt to kill Jake fails because Terry intervenes. She later visits Bruce in the Batcave. Bruce reveals that he searched for her years earlier and tries to convince her that they could still be together. Andrea explains that they have different ways of dealing with criminals, saying, "I do things Batman can't. I always have." She abandons her second attempt to kill Jake after he accidentally dies from exposure to Joker venom. Andrea Beaumont, also known as the Phantasm, made her debut in the main DC comic book universe in Batman/Catwoman, a limited series written by Tom King and illustrated by Clay Mann. The first issue was published in December 2020. King and Mann had revealed the Phantasm's inclusion in the series in 2019 through an image posted on Twitter. The image showed Batman and Catwoman reflected in the Phantasm's weapon, along with the words "She awaits you" and the series title. The series features three different timelines. In the present-day story, Andrea's return threatens the relationship between Bruce Wayne and Selina Kyle, also known as Catwoman. Her presence raises questions about their personal lives and their identities as costumed crime-fighters. DC Comics described her return as a possible threat to Bruce and Selina's future. The Phantasm appears as a playable character in Lego DC Super-Villains through downloadable content. Andrea Beaumont appears in the video game Batman: Arkham Shadow, where she is voiced by Amber Hood. In 1993, Kenner released a Phantasm action figure to promote Batman: Mask of the Phantasm. The figure came with the mask and cloak removed, revealing the character's identity. This may have spoiled the film's plot twist for some audiences. The figure was later re-released as part of a "Rogues Gallery" box set, with the grey and black colors of the costume reversed. In 2016, DC Collectibles released another Phantasm action figure as part of its six-inch toy line based on Batman: The Animated Series. The figure was sold with a re-release of the Batman figure from the same line. It had more detailed sculpting and more movable joints than the earlier figure. However, it did not include an unmasked head showing Andrea Beaumont's face, which had been included with the four-inch figure.

Andrei Arsenyevich Tarkovsky (April 4, 1932 - December 29, 1986) was a Soviet movie director, writer and opera director. Tarkovksy is listed as one of the 100 filmmakers best liked by movie critics. He received critical acclaim for directing such movies as Andrei Rublev, Solaris and Stalker. Tarkovsky also did a lot of work as a screenwriter, movie editor and theater director. He was also important as a movie theorist. He directed most of his movies in the Soviet Union, with the exception of his last two movies which were produced in Italy and Sweden. His movies are characterized by Christian spirituality and metaphysical themes. Other things that are typical for his movies are extremely long takes, the lack of conventional dramatic structure and plot, and memorable images of exceptional beauty. Tarkovsky died of lung cancer in Paris, at age 54.

Andrew G. Vajna (born András György Vajna; August 1, 1944 – January 20, 2019) was a Hungarian-American movie producer. He was born in Budapest. Vajna studied at the University of California, Los Angeles. He was known for his works in Nixon, Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines and Medicine Man. Vajna died at his home in Budapest following a long illness on January 20, 2019, aged 74.

Andrew Lesnie [[Australian Cinematographers Society (1 January 1956 – 27 April 2015) was an Australian movie cinematographer. He was best known as the cinematographer for The Lord of the Rings trilogy (2001–2003) and its prequel The Hobbit trilogy (2012–2014), both directed by New Zealand director Peter Jackson. He received the Academy Award for Best Cinematography for his work on The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring in 2002. He also worked on I Am Legend (2007) and The Water Diviner (2014). Lesnie was born in Sydney, New South Wales. He died from a heart attack on 27 April 2015 in Sydney, aged 59.

Andrew Marton (born Endre Marton; 26 January 1904 – 7 January 1992) was a Hungarian-American movie director. In his career, he directed 39 movies and television programs. He was known for directing Ben Hur (1959).
Andrew Christopher Stanton (born December 3, 1965) is an American movie director, producer, screenwriter and voice actor. He began working at Pixar in 1990.

Android 18 is a female character in the manga series Dragon Ball and the anime Dragon Ball Z. She is an android created by Dr. Gero to kill Goku. Android 18 is a beautiful blonde woman of average height and build she has blue eyes, and wears golden hoop earrings in both ears when she first appeared in Dragon Ball Z she wears a blue demin and skirt with a RR (Red Ribbon) logo. She also wears dark blue tights, a brown belt, brown boots and a black skirt that has white and black striped long sleeve. After the defeat of Cell she wears pale blue buttoned up demin vest, white jeans, red hoop earrings along with a red bracelet on her left hand and black flip flops. Android 18 was originally a human along with her twin brother Android 17. She and her brother 17 were delinquents until the scientist Dr. Gero kidnapped them and reconstruct them into superhumans (androids). Android 18's personality is portrayed as calm, cool and confident with some sarcasm. During her early appearances in Dragon Ball Z she was arrogant and usually annoyed by her brother Android 17's wild behavior. After the defeat of Cell, Android 18 settled down and married Krillin. They have a daughter named Marron. In the Buu arc, her involvement was minimal and could be frequently seen with the other Z Fighters at Kami's lookout. Android 18 also appears in spin-offs Dragon Ball GT and Dragon Ball Super. In Dragon Ball GT. Android 18 appears in several Dragon Ball Z movies and videos games. She appears in Dragon Ball movies like Super Android 13, Bio-Broly, Battle of Gods, Resurrection F and in video games like Dragon Ball Z Budokai Tenkaichi series, Dragon Ball Z Raging Blast 1 and 2 etc.

Andromeda (formally titled Gene Roddenberry's Andromeda) is a Canadian-American science fiction television series. Between 2000 and 2005, 110 episodes were produced. Each episode runs for about 40 minutes. The series is loosely based on a Star Trek related theme. It is based on material by Gene Roddenberry. His widow, Majel Barrett, helped produce it. As of 2021, Andromeda is one of two TV series (the other is Earth: Final Conflict) based on ideas Roddenberry had as early as the 1960s and 1970s. Roddenberry died in 1991, nine years before the series premiere. The name "Dylan Hunt" was used for the hero of two TV pilots Roddenberry had produced in the mid-1970s, Genesis II, and Planet Earth. Both had a similar setting.

Andrzej Witold Wajda (6 March 1926 – 9 October 2016) was a Polish movie director, movie producer, and screenwriter. He is known for his works in A Generation, Kanał, Ashes and Diamonds, Man of Iron, The Promised Land, The Maids of Wilko, and in Katyń. He won an Honorary Academy Award in 2000. Wajda was born in Suwałki, Poland. He studied at the Łódź Film School. Wajda was married four times, first three ended in divorce. He had a daughter. Wajda died of respiratory failure on 9 October 2016 at a hospital in Warsaw, aged 90.

Andrzej Żuławski (; 22 November 1940 – 17 February 2016) was a Polish movie director and writer. He was born in Lwów, Poland (now Ukraine). In the late 1950s, he studied filmmaking in France. His second movie The Devil (1972) was banned in Poland, and Żuławski went to France. After the success of That Most Important Thing: Love in 1975, he returned to Poland where he spent two years making On the Silver Globe (1988). After that, Żuławski moved to France where he became known for controversial and violent art-house movies. Żuławski is also known for his work with actresses including Romy Schneider, Isabelle Adjani and Sophie Marceau. Żuławski died of pancreatic cancer in Warsaw on 17 February 2016. He was aged 75.

András Kovács (20 June 1925 – 11 March 2017) was a Hungarian movie director and screenwriter. He directed 30 movies between 1961 and 1996. His 1968 movie The Lost Generation was entered into the 6th Moscow International Film Festival. His 1978 movie A ménesgazda was entered into the 29th Berlin International Film Festival. His 1981 movie Temporary Paradise won the Silver Prize at the 12th Moscow International Film Festival. His 1985 movie The Red Countess was entered into the 14th Moscow International Film Festival. Kovács was also a member of the jury at the 5th Moscow International Film Festival in 1967 and the 1976 Cannes Film Festival. Kovács died in Budapest, Hungary on 11 March 2017, aged 91.

André, Baron Delvaux (21 March 1926 – 4 October 2002) was a Belgian movie director. He is widely called the founder of the Belgian national cinema. Born in Heverlee, he died in Valencia, Spain. He received the Magritte Honorary Award at the Magritte Awards 2011. 1988 L'Oeuvre au noir (after Marguerite Yourcenar's book). Entered into the 1988 Cannes Film Festival. 1985 BABEL OPERA, ou la répétition de Don Juan de Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart 1983 Benvenuta (with Vittorio Gassman, Fanny Ardant, Françoise Fabian and Mathieu Carrière) (after Suzanne Lilar's book La Confession Anonyme) 1980 To Woody Allen, from Europe with love 1979 Een vrouw tussen hond en wolf (Femme entre chien et loup) 1975 Met Dieric Bouts (Avec Dieric Bouts) 1971 Rendez-vous à Bray (after Julien Gracq's novel, Le roi Cophetua) 1968 Un soir un train (with Yves Montand, Anouk Aimée, François Beukelaers) (after Johan Daisne's book De trein der traagheid) 1966 Derrière l'écran (Achter het scherm) 1965 De Man die zijn haar kort liet knippen (L'homme au crâne rasé) after Johan Daisne's book 1958 Cinéma, bonjour!

Andy's Adventures is a British preschool television series that ran on CBeebies for six seasons since February 13, 2012: volumes involved adventures: including wild in 2012, dinosaur in 2014, prehistoric in 2016, safari in 2018, aquatic in 2020, global in 2023.

Andrés Muschietti (; born 26 August 1973), usually credited as Andy Muschietti, is an Argentine movie director and screenwriter. He is best known for directing the 2013 horror movie Mama and the It duology starting with It: Chapter One (2017) and the 2019 sequel It: Chapter Two. He also directed the 2023 DC Extended Universe movie The Flash and will direct Batman: The Brave and the Bold DC Universe movie.

Andrew Clement "Andy" Serkis (born 20 April 1964) is an English movie, television, stage, voice actor, comedian, movie producer, and writer who is known for his roles in The Lord of the Rings movie series, King Kong, Rise of the Planet of the Apes, and in The Adventures of Tintin. He has won two Saturn Award in 2002 and in 2011 and a Screen Actors Guild Award in 2003. Serkis played Alfred Pennyworth in the 2022 crime-thriller movie The Batman. Serkis was born on 20 April 1964 in Ruislip, Middlesex, England. He studied at St Benedict's School, Ealing, Lancaster University, and in The County College. Serkis has been married to Lorraine Ashbourne since 2002. They have three children. Serkis has won 15 top awards for his portrayal of Gollum and his other work in movies, television and stage acting.

Anees Bazmee is an Indian movie director, producer, and screenwriter, known for his works in Hindi cinema. The first movie Bazmee directed was Hulchul in 1995. His first commercial success came in 1998 with the movie Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha, one of the highest-grossing Bollywood movies of the year. He achieved further success as well as recognition by directing the top-grossing comedies including No Entry (2005), Welcome (2007), Singh Is Kinng (2008), Ready (2011) and Welcome Back (2015), Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 (2022) and also received praise for directing the moderately successful romantic thriller Deewangee (2002).

Angel is a spin-off from the American television series Buffy the Vampire Slayer. Angel has a darker feel than Buffy, and at times did better in the U.S. Nielsen Ratings than Buffy. The series was created by Buffys creator Joss Whedon along with David Greenwalt. It first aired in October of 1999. Like Buffy, it was produced by Whedon's production company, Mutant Enemy. The series tells the story of the vampire Angel. Angel had his soul returned to him as punishment for killing a gypsy girl. This made him tormented by all the bad things he had done. During the first four seasons of the show, he works as a private detective in a fiction version of Los Angeles, California. There, he and a variety of others work to "help the helpless" and "save the souls" of those who had lost their way. This usually meant fighting evil demons or humans that worked with demons (the law firm Wolfram and Hart). He also had to fight his own violent nature. (Not all "demons" in the Angel universe are evil beings.) The fifth season saw Angel taking over as the person in charge of the evil law firm Wolfram and Hart. This was done to try to fight evil from the inside. Several years before the Angel first showed on television, writer Joss Whedon created the idea behind Buffy the Vampire Slayer to change the Hollywood formula of "the little blonde girl who goes into a dark alley and gets killed in every horror movie." Whedon was not happy with the way that the Buffy idea was first done in the 1992 movie, Buffy the Vampire Slayer,. He was given the chance to do the story better with the television series of the same name. The early years of the series were about the life of Buffy Summers, a high-school aged vampire slayer, and her group of friends in Sunnydale (a fictional small town in California). The supernatural parts in the series took the place of the real problems that are a part of adolescence and young adulthood. The character Angel was first seen in the first episode. He became a regular cast member during the second/third seasons. In the fictional universe created by Buffy (the Buffyverse), Angel was born in 18th century Ireland. After being turned into a soulless immortal vampire, he became very well known for the evil things he did. Over 100 years later, Angel killed a gypsy girl. Her family punished him by returning his soul. He felt a very large amount of guilt for what he had done over all those years. Angel eventually began on a path of redemption. He hoped that he might make up for his past by doing good deeds. In the Buffy third season final episode, Angel leaves Sunnydale for Los Angeles to continue his path of redemption without Buffy. Whedon believed that "Angel was the one character who was bigger than life in the same way that Buffy was, a kind of superhero." While the main idea behind Buffy was "High school as a horror movie" in small-town America, Greenwalt and Whedon wanted to make Angel into a different "gritty, urban show". Joss Whedon and David Greenwalt created a short video, often called the "Unaired Angel pilot" for the WB Network. The idea for the series was a new version of the old detective genre. On Valentine's Day, 2004, the WB Network said that Angel would not be brought back for a sixth season. Joss Whedon posted a message on a popular fan site, The Bronze: Beta, in which he showed his surprise. He said he was "heartbroken". Fans created letter-writing campaigns and online petitions. They tried to get other networks, UPN mainly (the network that picked up Buffy), to pick up the show. Angels final episode, "Not Fade Away", aired on the WB May 19, 2004. Angel (David Boreanaz) – Vampire over two hundred years old. He was known as Angelus during the time he was causing evil across Europe. He was cursed with a soul which gave him a conscience and guilt for the centuries of murder and torture he had done. Angel moves to L.A. in search of redemption. Cordelia Chase (Charisma Carpenter) – At Sunnydale, Cordelia was a shallow cheerleader. She is changed by the loss of her parents' financial support and her not becoming a star in L.A. She joins Angel Investigations to help Angel. Allen Francis Doyle (Glenn Quinn) – He was born to a human mother and a demon father in Dublin, Ireland. He became a messenger for the Powers That Be. Wesley Wyndam-Pryce (Alexis Denisof) – His failure as a Watcher and being fired from the Watchers' Council led Wesley to hunt demons. He joined Angel and went on to lead Angel Investigations. Charles Gunn (J. August Richards) - He grew up in a part of Los Angeles where the police were afraid to go. Gunn grew up fighting vampires. He did not trust Angel at first but eventually joins the group. Winifred "Fred" Burkle (Amy Acker) – A young Texan physicist, she is trapped in a world where humans are enslaved by demons for five years. Angel saved her and brought her back to L.A. Connor (Vincent Kartheiser) – Connor is born in Los Angeles, California. He was a "miracle", a human child born of two vampires, Angel and Darla. He was taken to a hell dimension. He spent his childhood and much of his adolescence there. He came back to L.A. as an angry young man. Lorne (Andy Hallett) – Lorne was a demon. Lorne lived in L.A. as the host of a Caritas, a violence-free demon-friendly karaoke bar. He can see into people's souls when they sing. His full name is Krevlorneswath of the "Deathwok Clan". Spike (James Marsters) – A vampire who roamed Europe with Angel in the late 19th century. He joins the team after getting back his own soul. Illyria (Amy Acker) – One of the Old Ones. She was one of the first demons who ruled the area that now includes California. Long ago, Illyria's corpse was placed in a stone sarcophagus. Her powers were taken away and put in jewels on her coffin. Illyria came back by infecting the body of a human (Winifred Burkle). Harmony Kendall (Mercedes McNab) – At high school, she was a member of Cordelia Chase's popular clique, the "Cordettes". During her graduation, she is turned into a vampire. She kept her "bubbly" personality, and many of her bad personality traits. This made her very bad as a vampire. She decided to get a job with evil law firm Wolfram and Hart as a secretary. Angel is a fictional vampire that appears in the television series Buffy the Vampire Slayer and is the main character of the spin-off Angel. He was played by David Boreanaz. Liam of Ireland was sired by a female vampire and became known as Angelus. He would later sire Spike and work alongside Drusilla and the Master. On 1898, he killed a Romani and a mystic placed a spell where she restored his soul, making him feel guilty. Now known as Angel, he moved to America and stayed at Sunnydale. As Angelus, he is considered one of the best Big Bads of Buffy the Vampire Slayer.

Ang Lee (born 23 October 1954) is a Taiwanese movie director. He has directed movies like Eat Drink Man Woman, Sense and Sensibility, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Hulk and Brokeback Mountain. He has won Academy Awards (Oscars) for Brokeback Mountain and 'Life of Pi'. Ang Lee was born in 1954 in a town called Chaozhou, Pingtung, Taiwan He went to the National Tainan First Senior High School where his father was the principal, and then to the National Arts School. He graduated in 1975. In 1979, he went to the United States and studied theatre at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. He got his Master's degree at New York University, and he worked there with another famous director called Spike Lee.
Angel is a 1982 Irish drama movie directed by first time director Neil Jordan and starring Stephen Rea, Veronica Quilligan, Honor Heffernan, Alan Devlin, Peter Caffrey, Gerard McSorley, Ray McAnally.

Angel Beats! is an anime series. It was made by Jun Maeda. It ran from April 3, 2010 until June 26, 2010. P.A. Works and Aniplex both produced it. There were two original video animations after the show ended. Angel Beats! Stairway to Heaven was released on December 22, 2010 and Angel Beats! Hell's Kitchen was released on June 24, 2015. There was a visual novel of the anime released on June 26, 2015 called Angel Beats! 1st Beat. The show was popular and well liked. The awards jury for the 14th Japan America Arts Festival in 2010 chose the show as a recommended work. Episode six of the show was able to break the record for a 4.9% rating in MBS station's "Anime Shower" block. The Blu-ray discs sold very well. All seven volumes sold within the top 3 on the Oricon chart. The series is about Yuzuru Otonashi, a boy who is sent to a high school in the afterlife and has lost his memory. He joins a group called the Afterlife Battlefront after he meets a girl named Yuri Nakamura. Nakamura tells Otonashi that the group and her fight against an unseen God and a student council president named Kanade Tachibana. After he gets hypnotized by Ayato Naik, the deputy president of the school, Otonashi begins to regain his memories. After Kanade gets demoted, Otonashi becomes friends with her. She tells him that her job is to help students move on from limbo in the afterlife and find peace. Otonashi tells her that he wants to help the rest of the Afterlife Battlefront move on. After he helps them, he tells Kanade that he loves her. Kanade says that Otonashi is the donor of her heart and helped her live longer. She then moves on.

"Angel's Eye" is a 2000 song by American hard rock band Aerosmith. It was released as a promotional single to the movie Charlie's Angels. It received heavy rotation on rock radio and made number 4 on the Billboard Mainstream Rock Tracks chart.

Angad Aulakh is an American filmmaker. His feature directorial debut Autumn Lights, released in theaters in North America on October 21, 2016. He produced the film for his company Last Carnival with Guy Kent. Aulakh produced Autumn Lights for his company Last Carnival with Guy Kent, alongside Ashley M. Kent, Davíd Óskar Ólafsson and Árni Filippusson, producers of Ragnar Bragason's Metalhead and David Gordon Green's Prince Avalanche. Aulakh was nominated for Best Director at the 2017 Riviera International Film Festival for Autumn Lights alongside Xavier Dolan for It's Only the End of the World, winner Amanda Kernell for Baden Baden and Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Ciro Guerra for Embrace of the Serpent. The film was also nominated for the Grand Jury Prize for Best Picture, Aulakh sharing the nomination with producers Guy Kent, Ashley M. Kent, David Oskar Olafsson, and Arni Filippusson. Autumn Lights was nominated by Norway's Cinema Scandinavia for Best Picture in Fall 2016.

Angela's Ashes is a 1999 British and American historical drama movie. It is based on a memoir of the same name by Frank McCourt. It was co-produced between the United States, United Kingdom and Ireland. The movie is set in and around Limerick. However, many scenes were filmed in Cork. Angela's Ashes had a $25 million budget. But it only made $13,042,112 in the United States. That made the movie a box office bomb. The movie has a 52% "rotten" rating on the Rotten Tomatoes. However, the audience rated the movie at 82%. Roger Ebert gave Angela's Ashes two and a half stars. Angel Has Fallen is a 2019 American action thriller movie directed by Ric Roman Waugh. It is about a US Secret Service agent being framed for a drone strike on the President of the United States by a group of mercenaries working for the Vice President. It is the third movie in the Fallen movie series, following Olympus Has Fallen (2013) and London Has Fallen (2016). The movie stars are Gerard Butler, Morgan Freeman, Jada Pinkett Smith, Lance Reddick, Tim Blake Nelson, Piper Perabo, Nick Nolte, and Danny Huston. The movie was released in the United States on August 23, 2019, by Lionsgate. It received mixed reviews from critics. It made $147.5 million worldwide.

Angel on the Right (, translit. Farishtai kitfi rost) is a 2002 Tajik Swiss French Italian comedy-drama movie directed by Jamshed Usmonov and starring Uktamoi Miyasarova, Maruf Pulodzoda, Kova Tilavpur, Mardonkul Kulbobo, Malohat Maqsumova.

Angel and the Badman is a 1947 American romantic western movie directed by James Edward Grant and starring John Wayne, Gail Russell, Harry Carey, Bruce Cabot, Irene Rich, Lee Dixon. It was distributed by Republic Pictures.

Angela Bettis (born January 9, 1973) is an American movie, television, and stage actress. She was born in Austin, Texas. In the 2002 telefilm Carrie, Angela, Jodelle Ferland and the baby replaced Sissy Spacek for being Carrie.

Angela Noelle Schrute (née Martin; formerly Lipton) is a fictional character from the US television series The Office played by American actress Angela Kinsey. She is an original character. She marries Dwight Schrute in the series. Martin is the head of the accounting department at the Scranton branch of the fictitious paper distribution company Dunder Mifflin. Angela is often negative and frowns upon her coworkers all the time. She is a critic of Pam Beesley's and Jim Halpert's relationship.

Angela Valdes, played by Lela Loren, is a character from the Starz original television drama series Power. She was a Latina federal agent whose mission was to solve the mystery behind the infamous "Ghost" until she realized she had been in love with him the entire time. Angela Valdes was caught in a crossfire and took a bullet for her lover James "Ghost" St. Patrick (Omari Hardwick). She was mistakenly murdered by Tommy Egan (Joseph Sikora) after Egan found out Ghost was working with Valdes to get him arrested for the murder of his father Tony Teresi (William Sadler). Angela Valdes was born and raised in Jamaica, Queens where she met her childhood friends, Tommy Egan and James St. Patrick. They attended to the same school where Angela dated James. She moved from Queens to further her studies. After almost 20 years fate led her to her high school lover in New York City. Angela was the younger sister of Paz Valdes (Elizabeth Rodriguez) and the daughter of Nestor Valdes (Jamie Tirelli).

Angelina Ballerina is a British preschool animated children's television series, based on the Angelina Ballerina series of children's books by author Katharine Holabird and illustrator Helen Craig. The series is about Angelina Mouseling, a young mouse who loves dancing ballet, her family, and her classmates. Finty Williams performed the voice of Angelina, and her real-life mother Judi Dench performed the voice of Miss Lilly, her old ballet teacher. The show had 39 15-minute-long episodes, as well as three longer specials. The series was produced by HiT Entertainment and Grand Slamm Children's Films. It aired on the CITV block of ITV in the United Kingdom, and on Nick Jr, PBS Kids (2002–2009) and PBS Kids Sprout (2005–2011) in the United States, where it was presented by Connecticut Public Television.

Angelina Ballerina: The Next Steps is an animated musical preschool television series that originally aired on Nick Jr. and PBS Kids (produced by HIT Entertainment and WNET, events of the previous series), was ran from September 5, 2009 to November 13, 2010.
Angels & Insects is a 1995 romantic drama movie. The movie stars Mark Rylance, Kristin Scott Thomas and Patsy Kensit. It got good reviews from the critics.

Court no Naka no Tenshi-tachi is a Japanese erotic visual novel. It was developed by Pinpai and published by Pink Pineapple. It was released on September 22, 1999 for Windows. There is a four-episode animated series based on this visual novel. It was released from October 27, 2000 to January 25, 2002. In North America the first two episodes were localized as Angels in the Court by NuTech Digital. Court no Naka no Tenshi-tachi was published into a two volume novel series by KSS Books. It was written by Muto Yasuyuki. It is based on his screenplay for the anime. The books were published on August 30, 2001 and July 20, 2002.

Angels is a British television seasonal drama series about student nurses. It was broadcast by the BBC between 1975 and 1983. It was described as the "Z-Cars of nursing". From 1979 the show changed to a seasonal twice-weekly soap opera format. The show's title came from the name of the hospital where the first series was set. This was St. Angela's in Battersea. In the 1980s this was changed to Heath Green Hospital in Birmingham. The series was devised by Paula Milne. Early producers included Morris Barry and Ron Craddock. The first episode was directed by Julia Smith. She became the show's producer in 1979. Her script editor on the later series was Tony Holland. Filming took place at St James' Hospital in Balham, London. This has since been demolished. Location filming for the fictional Heath Green Hospital took place at Walsgrave Hospital in Coventry. This has since been demolished and replaced by University Hospital Coventry. Julia Smith enlisted Tony Holland as the Angels script editor after the show became a twice-weekly soap. In the 1980s Smith and Holland created EastEnders. Writers on its first series included Jill Hyem, Anne Valery and Adele Rose. Hyem and Valery later co-wrote Tenko. The series included some young actors who would later become better known. These include Fiona Fullerton, Érin Geraghty, Lesley Dunlop, Julie Dawn Cole, Angela Bruce, Clare Clifford and Pauline Quirke. Additionally, Kathryn Apanowicz, Shirley Cheriton and Judith Jacob all later appeared in EastEnders. Mamta Kaash played a key role in the hospital drama Casualty. The guitar-driven theme tune, similar to American police dramas of the time, was called Motivation. It was composed and performed by Alan Parker. Angels, tackled issues such as contraception, alcoholism and promiscuity as part of the nurses' lives. Angels received criticism for its unglamorous depiction of the nursing profession. Angels tried to be realistic and authentic. Each actress was required to work on a real hospital ward to gain experience. Some TV tie-in novels were published to coincide with the series. Angels by Paula Milne & Leslie Duxbury, Pan Books/BBC Books, 1975. Flights of Angels by Paula Milne, Pan Books/BBC Books, 1976. Includes novelisations of the Season 2 episodes Vocation and Walkabout. New Angels by Paul Milne, BBC Books, 1978. Angel Katy by Leah Harrow, Dragon Books, 1979. On 18 March 2013 Simply Media released the Series 1 (fifteen episodes) of Angels on DVD. Series 2 was released in September 2014.

Angels in the Outfield is a 1951 American family baseball comedy movie directed by Clarence Brown and starring Paul Douglas, Janet Leigh, Keenan Wynn, Donna Corcoran, Lewis Stone, Bruce Bennett, Marvin Kaplan and Ellen Corby. It was distributed by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and was remade in 1994 by Walt Disney Pictures.
Angels in the Outfield is a 1994 American family sports fantasy comedy-drama movie directed by William Dear. It is a remake of the 1951 movie of the same name.

Angels in the Endzone is a 1997 American fantasy sports movie directed by Gary Nadeau and starring Christopher Lloyd. It is a sequel to the 1994 movie Angels in the Outfield. The movie is about a high school football team that lacks skill.
Angels in the Infield is a 2000 Disney television movie directed by Robert King and starring Patrick Warburton, Brittney Irvin, David Alan Grier, and Kurt Fuller.

Angels & Demons is a 2009 American mystery thriller movie directed by Ron Howard. The film stars Tom Hanks as Robert Langdon. The story is based on the novel of the same name by Dan Brown. it is the sequel to the 2006 movie The Da Vinci Code. The film follows Langdon as he helps investigate a murder at CERN and a plot that threatens the Vatican during a papal conclave. The movie was released on May 15, 2009, and was distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing. After a scientist is found dead at CERN in Switzerland, a dangerous substance called antimatter disappears. An Illuminati symbol burned into the dead scientist's body makes people think the secret group still exists. Robert Langdon is called to help solve the crime. The story takes place during the papal conclave in Rome and follows Langdon as he searches for answers and tries to stop more murders. Ewan McGregor as Camerlengo Patrick McKenna (Carlo Ventresca in the book) Stellan Skarsgård as Commander Maximilian Richter Pierfrancesco Favino as Inspector Ernesto Olivetti Carmen Argenziano as Father Silvano Bentivoglio Marco Fiorini as Cardinal Baggia / Pope Lucas In 2003, Sony Pictures got the film rights to Angels & Demons and The Da Vinci Code. After the success of The Da Vinci Code, Sony hired Akiva Goldsman to write a script for Angels & Demons. The film had mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, the film holds a moderate score, with critics saying it is an exciting ride but not always believable. Audiences gave more mixed opinions. Filming was planned to start in early 2008 but was delayed by the 2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike. David Koepp later rewrote the script. Filming began on 4 June 2008 in Rome. Other parts were shot at Sony Pictures Studios in Los Angeles. Some church interiors were built on sets because the Catholic Church did not allow filming in its churches. The Palace of Caserta stood in for the interior of the Vatican in some scenes. The Biblioteca Angelica was used to represent the Vatican Library. Some leaders of the Catholic Church criticized the film. The Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano said the Church could not approve the movie. There were calls for a boycott by some Church figures. However, past calls to boycott similar films had little effect on audience interest.

Angie is a 1994 American romantic comedy-drama movie. The movie is about the title character, whom some people have troubles understanding. Geena Davis plays the title character. Aida Turturro plays Tina, and James Gandolfini plays Vinnie. The movie received mixed reviews. It didn't make much money.

Anger Management is a 2003 American slapstick comedy movie directed by Peter Segal. It was written by David S. Dorfman. It stars Adam Sandler, Jack Nicholson, Marisa Tomei, John Turturro, and Woody Harrelson. It was produced by Revolution Studios. It has cameo appearances of Rudy Giuliani, Bob Sheppard, and Derek Jeter. It was released to positive reviews on April 11, 2003.

Angoor is a 1982 Indian Hindi-language comedy movie. It was directed by Gulzar. The movie stars Sanjeev Kumar and Deven Verma in double roles. It is a remake of the 1968 Indian movie Do Dooni Char. That movie was a remake of the 1963 Bengali language movie Bhranti Bilas. It was based on Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's Bengali novel by the same name. That book was based on Shakespeare's play The Comedy of Errors. Angoor was remade by Rohit Shetty as Cirkus. All of the characters in the move are innocent. Destiny plays the main role in bringing all characters to one place. This is different from most movies that have characters who are not innocent and make false statements to fool other characters. The story is based on Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors. This is a story of two pair of identical twins and mistaken identities. Sanjeev Kumar in a double role as twin brothers Ashok Tilak and Ashok Tilak. Moushmi Chatterjee as Sudha Tilak, Ashok's wife Deven Verma in a double role as twin brothers Bahadur and Bahadur. Yunus Parvez as Mansoor Miyan, Chhedilal's worker T. P. Jain as Ganeshilal, a diamond merchant Utpal Dutt as Raj Tilak, Ashok's father (Cameo) Arjun Chakraborty as an office assistant under Ashok Tilak The DVD version of the movie was released by IndiaWeekly under its own label.

Angry Birds Toons is a Finnish animated television series based on the Angry Birds series of games created by Rovio Entertainment. The series was first shown on Cartoon Network Canada. It began on March 16, 2013. At first, the episodes were 2 minutes and 48 seconds long, and later became 2 minutes 47 seconds. There are 52 episodes in the first season, and 26 in the second and third seasons. The characters in Angry Birds Toons are birds, pigs, and other animals. None of the characters in the series say anything. Birds chirp, pigs grunt. But these sounds, including shouts, groans, growls, squeaks, squeals, laughter, etc., are being published by people, Finnish actors (often the authors of the series themselves are scriptwriters, directors, composers). Red is the clear leader among the birds. He takes special care of eggs, devoting all his free time to them. He tries to destroy pigs at the first opportunity. He made his first appearance in the episode "Chuck Time". Jay, Jake, and Jim are three twin brothers who are cheerful and active chicks. They love pranks, and their actions often lead to trouble. They like to make fun of other birds and pigs. They made their first appearance in the episode "Full Metal Chuck". Chuck is fast and athletic, a bit vain and arrogant. He has the ability to accelerate so that everything around he slows down. He made his first appearance in "Chuck Time". Matilda is caring, kind, and has cooking skills, although sometimes her cooking can only be fed to pigs. Despite her kindness, Matilda can get very angry. She made her first appearance in the episode "Egg Sounds". Bomb is fun and aggressive at the same time. He loves ice cream, corn and knows how to explode. He wants to do "heroic" deeds, but only succeeds sometimes. He made his first appearance in the episode "Off Duty". Bubbles is cheerful and friendly, very fond of sweets, and when candy is taken away from him, he becomes enraged and does anything to get the candy back. Like the Bluebirds, they are a child. Can swell up to the size of Terence. He made his first appearance in the Halloween special "Night of the Living Pork". Terence, as shown in this series, sullen, stubborn, and stern, even a little wild. Calm and solid as a wall. But despite this, he sometimes smiles. He made his first appearance in the episode "Gardening with Terence". The Eggs are the unborn children of birds. According to the plot, pigs want to steal them and cook scrambled eggs from them. Each of the adult birds wants to instil their own character in their offspring. They made their first appearance in the episode "Egg Sounds". Minion Pigs are the main population of Pig City, loyal servants of the King, ready to carry out any order. They are very sociable and social, they love parties and celebrations. They do not recognize high-ranking persons without their headdress. They made their first appearance in the episode "Where's My Crown?" King Pig is the leader of the pigs. He dreams of getting bird eggs and making scrambled eggs from them. Greedy, stupid, fond of sweets. I'm used to the fact that everyone obeys his orders. Sometimes he behaves like a child. He also made his first appearance in "Where's My Crown?" Corporal Pig is a pig with a helmet. He leads the minions and is also the head of the Pig King's guards. He constantly tries to steal bird eggs, but all his attempts and plans fail. He, once more, made his first appearance in "Where's My Crown?" Foreman Pig is the head of security and Pig City's foreman. He wants to get a promotion from the King of Pigs, he is ready to do anything for this. He made his first appearance in "Slappy-Go-Lucky". Chef Pig is the head chef and advisor to the King of Pigs. He dreams of taking the crown from him and becoming the ruler of Pig City. He made his first appearance in "True Blue?". Chronicler Pig is the Chronicler, Priest, Judge, and Master of Ceremonies of Pig City, one of the Pig King's most loyal servants. He is very intelligent and calm. He made his first appearance in "Love is in the Air". Professor Pig is a genius scientist and inventor, though his creations don't always work properly. He dreams of birds and pigs living in harmony. He made his first appearance in the episode "Slappy-Go-Lucky". Fat Pig is a strong but narcissistic, arrogant and cowardly pig. He can sing very loudly. He made his first appearance in the episode "El Porkador!". Hambo is a tenacious and brave fighter, a loyal apprentice of the Corporal. However, he is inattentive and a bit stupid. He made his first appearance in the episode of the same name "Hambo". Muscle Pig is a pumped-up pig who is used to solving all problems with his immense strength. He loves to fight, but on the condition that he wins. He can't stand losing. He made his first appearance in the episode "Hamshank Redemption". Anguirus is a fictional monster who appears in movies in the Godzilla series. He is a very large, mutated ankylosaurus.
